analysis:
The only file in this batch is CHANGELOG.md, which is documentation only. Units :8 and :9 are the base text (lines 1381-1756, historical release notes); unit :10 is the head text (lines 1-230, new unreleased entries). No executable source, authorization logic or configuration is in these units, so I found no concrete regression to cite.

The head entries describe behaviour changes whose code is not supplied here, so the next pass must review the real source:
- CHANGELOG.md lines 3-7 (Autopilot daily earnings floor) describe a new financial surface touching A-009 and TB-006/TB-008. It adds a separately funded pool, an opt-in baseline taken from the preceding 168 hours including sponsored inference, and admin funding and baseline-repair endpoints. Payments are stated to default off. Reviewers should check for wash-trading or self-routing inflation of the baseline, idempotency and double payment across machine aliases, admin authorization, and erasure/archive coverage (the entry itself says archives do not yet cover the new tables).
- Lines 76-81 (migration budgets, early App Attest production validation, soft-delete mutation gate defaulting to false) touch TB-011 and T-059. Check the 503 `soft_delete_mutations_disabled` path and the claim that production env refresh preserves explicit opt-ins.
- Lines 87-105 (account erasure) touch T-059. Check the confirm token, the repeated email and wallet checks, and the outbox handling of Stripe IDs.
- Lines 111-113 (removing PII from logs) bear on T-058.
- Line 229 (stripping top-level user, metadata, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies) overlaps the caller-field minimization boundary in the canonical context and T-003. The claim that nested content is preserved is correct and consistent with that boundary.
- Lines 13-18 (machine-scoped Autopilot and lease grants) touch TB-002 and TB-011 final-dispatch authorization.

The claims are consistent with the existing threat-model assumptions. I cannot verify them against code in this batch.
